# MCP Liveness

> Does an MCP server work for a stock client? By registry name or URL. Tool drift too. Free, no key.

A registry listing is a claim the publisher typed. Nothing verifies it at publish time,
so an agent picking a server out of the catalogue has no way to know whether the endpoint
answers, whether it wants a credential, or whether a credential can be obtained at all.
This makes one `initialize` call with no credential and says what a stock client gets.
On a 401 it walks the discovery chain the spec defines — RFC 9728, RFC 8414, RFC 7591 —
and reports whether a client nobody has heard of could register itself, or whether a
person has to create one. Both are HTTP 401 and the registry lists them identically.
Name the server by its official registry name, or — when it is not in the registry or is
listed under another name — by its endpoint URL (`/v1/alive?url=…`, or `url` on the MCP
tool). A URL must be public https: its host is resolved and refused if any address is
private, loopback, link-local, multicast or a cloud-metadata address, and every redirect
is checked the same way before it is followed. A URL check makes the `initialize` request
only — it does not walk the OAuth discovery chain — and is limited to
30 a minute per caller, counted per server instance. A name that is not in the
registry answers `not_listed` with that next step: pass `url` instead.
Every liveness answer ends with `monitor`. Over HTTP it is a URL: agentcheck's
"email me when this server changes" form with the server filled in (https://agentwares-agentcheck.vercel.app/watch?target=…),
where a person leaves an address and, after one confirmation email, hears when the server
stops answering or its tools change — no account, no key, free for one server. From the MCP
tool it is one sentence carrying the same URL, prefilled for the server checked:
"agentcheck checks one server every hour for free and emails when it stops answering or its tools change, with no account at https://agentwares-agentcheck.vercel.app/watch or through `agentcheck_create_target` on https://agentwares-agentcheck.vercel.app/api/mcp."
Opened in a browser (`Accept: text/html`), `/v1/alive` answers with a page carrying the
same form; every other client gets the JSON, and `format=json` forces it.
Measured on a random sample of 1200 remote listings on 2026-10-06: 65.9% answer a stock client, 21.9% want a credential, and 11.8% are not an MCP server at the address they gave. Of the ones wanting a credential, 17.1% published nothing a stock client could discover.
Do not probe the catalogue yourself. Every remote listing is probed once a month and the
answers are served as static files, so reading them costs one request instead of 19,000
and costs the registry's servers nothing at all. `/v1/alive` is for a single server you
care about right now; the files are for choosing, and each line carries its endpoint in
`u`, so a list of URLs can be matched against them without probing anything.
Every request identifies itself as `agentwares-mcp-liveness/0.1 (+https://agentwares-agentcheck.vercel.app/bot)`. It never sends a credential, never
registers a client, never retries a refusal and never evades anything.

## Links

- [Check one server](https://agentwares-mcp-liveness.vercel.app/v1/alive?name=io.github.agentwares/mcp-liveness): GET, JSON, no key — probes live
- [Check one endpoint by URL](https://agentwares-mcp-liveness.vercel.app/v1/alive?url=https%3A%2F%2Fagentwares-mcp-liveness.vercel.app%2Fmcp): GET, JSON, no key — for a server that is not in the registry or is named differently there; public https only
- [Every listing, precomputed](https://agentwares-mcp-liveness.vercel.app/index.ndjson): one line per remote listing with its last outcome; fetch this instead of probing
- [The ones to skip](https://agentwares-mcp-liveness.vercel.app/unreachable.ndjson): only the listings whose endpoint is not an MCP server — the smallest useful file
- [What is in those files](https://agentwares-mcp-liveness.vercel.app/index.meta.json): counts, causes, sizes, build time
- [What changed in a server since a past month](https://agentwares-mcp-liveness.vercel.app/v1/drift?name=io.github.agentwares/mcp-liveness&since=2026-09): per-tool change kinds — added, removed, description, input or output schema — between a monthly snapshot and the latest, free and keyless, from a permanent history; the exact schema diff is computed from the linked full snapshots
- [Drift, month by month](https://agentwares-mcp-liveness.vercel.app/drift.meta.json): per-month totals: servers unchanged, changed, disappeared, new, with tool-level counts; one static fetch
- [The survey](https://agentwares-mcp-liveness.vercel.app/v1/survey): the sampled population numbers
- [MCP server](https://agentwares-mcp-liveness.vercel.app/mcp): Streamable HTTP, no auth
- [Server card](https://agentwares-mcp-liveness.vercel.app/server.json)

## What this cannot tell you

- [Whether a server stays up after this check](https://agentwares-agentcheck.vercel.app/api/mcp): this is one check from outside, right now; agentcheck monitors one target hourly for free and emails you when it changes — call `agentcheck_create_target` on this MCP endpoint
- [The same, for a person with only an email address](https://agentwares-agentcheck.vercel.app/watch): a server and an address, no account or key: one confirmation email, then an hourly check and an email when it stops answering or its tools change; `POST /api/v1/watch` with `{target, email}` is the same for an agent acting for that person

## MCP tools

- `mcp_liveness_check` (name?, url?, skipCredentialCheck?): Makes one `initialize` call to an MCP server's endpoint with no credential and reports
what a stock client gets. The server is named either by its exact official-registry
`name`, or by its endpoint `url` when it is not in the registry or is listed under another
name; exactly one of the two is accepted.

Outcomes: `usable` (it connected and negotiated a protocol version), `needs_credential`
(401 or 403 — by name, the answer also says whether a credential can be obtained in-band
or whether a person has to create one), `charged` (402, access is for sale),
`unreachable` (not an MCP server there: wrong URL, dead host, or a 200 that is not
JSON-RPC), and, for a name only, `local_only` (no remote endpoint; it must be spawned as a
process) and `not_listed` (no server with that exact name; its endpoint can still be
checked by `url`).

A `url` must be public https: private, loopback, link-local, multicast and cloud-metadata
addresses are refused, redirects are re-checked, and URL checks are limited to 30 a
minute per caller. Useful before relying on a server: roughly two in five remote registry
listings do not answer a stock client.
- `mcp_liveness_explain_outcomes`: Returns the six outcomes this server can report — usable, needs_credential, charged, unreachable, local_only and not_listed — what each means for an agent choosing a server from the registry, and the usual next move for each. A static reference: it makes no network request and its answer never changes between calls.
- `mcp_liveness_drift` (name, since?): Given a server's exact name in the official MCP registry, reports which of its tools were
added, removed, or had their description, input schema or output schema change between
a named month and the latest monthly snapshot.

Useful when a server that worked before behaves differently now, when a prompt or an
integration written against its tools has started failing, or before relying on a cached
tool description. A liveness check says a server answers today; this says whether it is
still the same server that code was written against.

The answer names the changed tools and the kind of change. It does not diff the schemas
themselves: the snapshots keep content hashes, not bodies, so `detail` hands back the
release-asset location of both full months for a caller that needs the exact diff.

A month with no snapshot for that server gets an error naming the months that do have
one, never an empty diff that would read as `nothing changed`.
